# leanforge-mcp — Full LLM Context

MCP server for AI-driven formal proof search in Lean 4.
Based on AlphaProof Nexus (arXiv:2605.22763, DeepMind May 2026).

## Architecture

leanforge-mcp is a FastMCP 3.4 server. On startup, a lifespan context manager
creates three shared components: JobManager (SQLite persistence), LeanClient
(wraps `lake env lean` for Mathlib-aware compilation), and Runner (orchestrates
parallel proof search). These are stored in FastMCP lifespan context and
retrieved by tool handlers via `ctx.lifespan["runner"]`.

`submit_theorem` starts a background asyncio.Task and returns a job_id
immediately. The task runs `run_parallel_agents()` which spawns N independent
subagents. Each subagent loops: call LLM with current Lean file and last
compiler error -> parse search-replace response -> apply edit -> compile with
`lake env lean` -> feed output back to LLM. First subagent to produce a
sorry-free compile wins; others are cancelled. All attempts persist to SQLite.

## Why `lake env lean`, not `lean`

A bare `lean` invocation cannot resolve `import Mathlib`. Lean code must run
inside a Lake project with Mathlib dependencies and precompiled oleans on the
search path. The correct invocation is `lake env lean <file>`, which sets up
the full Lake project environment before invoking the compiler. A persistent
Lake workspace with Mathlib must be created once (one-time ~4GB download via
`lake exe cache get`).

## LLM tiers

Tier 1: local Ollama, deepseek-prover-v2:7b, free, ~15 tok/s on RTX 4090.
Tier 2: DeepSeek V4 Flash API, ~$0.001 per attempt.
Tier 3: Claude Fable 5, $50/M output, reserved for hard open problems.

Escalation is per-subagent and irreversible within a job. Thresholds
configurable in config.toml (default: tier 1->2 at turn 20, 2->3 at turn 60).

## Tools

### submit_theorem
Submit a theorem for formal proof search.
Input: statement (Lean 4 proposition), optional lean_stub (complete file with
sorry), optional hints (Mathlib theorem names), tier (1-3), parallel_agents
(1-16), max_turns (1-1000).
Returns: job_id (UUID string), status ("queued"), message.
Behavior: creates SQLite job record, starts background asyncio.Task, returns
immediately. Use get_proof_status to poll.

### submit_lean_file
Submit a complete Lean 4 file with sorry placeholders.
Input: lean_source (complete file with sorry), description, tier, parallel_agents,
max_turns.
Returns: job_id, sorry_count, message.
Use for: MiniF2F problem files, AlphaProof Nexus stub files from
google-deepmind/alphaproof-nexus-results.

### get_proof_status
Poll a proof search job.
Input: job_id (UUID string).
Returns: status (queued/running/complete/failed/cancelled/interrupted),
proof (complete Lean file if status=complete), latest_turn, latest_compiler_output,
latest_model.
Polling interval: 10-30 seconds for running jobs.

### list_attempts
Inspect proof search trajectory for a job.
Input: job_id, optional agent_index (filter to one subagent), last_n (default 10).
Returns: list of attempts with agent_index, turn, success, llm_model,
compiler_output (truncated to 400 chars).
Use for: understanding why search is stuck, inspecting what strategies were tried.

### list_jobs
List all jobs with status.
Input: optional status_filter (queued/running/complete/failed/cancelled/
interrupted), limit (default 20).
Returns: list of jobs with job_id, status, description, created_at.

### cancel_job
Cancel a running proof search job.
Input: job_id.
Returns: confirmation or current status if no live task found.

### validate_lean
Run the Lean 4 compiler on arbitrary source. No job tracking, no LLM.
Input: lean_source (Lean 4 code).
Returns: success (bool), proven (bool), has_sorry (bool), errors (list),
warnings (list).
Use for: testing a proof before submitting, debugging Lean syntax,
validating the compile pipeline works.

### get_mathlib_search
Search Mathlib4 for theorems by natural language.
Input: query (natural language description), limit (default 5).
Returns: list of {name, statement, module} for matching Mathlib theorems.
Use for: finding the right lemma name when the agent is stuck; pass result as
hints to submit_theorem.
Data source: LeanSearch API at leansearch.net.

## Typical agent workflow

Step 1: validate_lean("import Mathlib\nexample : 1 = 1 := rfl\n")
  -> {"proven": true} confirms the compile pipeline works.

Step 2: submit_theorem(statement="for all n : nat, 2 * sum(0..n) = n*(n+1)",
    tier=1, parallel_agents=4, max_turns=100)
  -> {"job_id": "abc-123", "status": "queued"}

Step 3: [wait 10-30 seconds]
  get_proof_status("abc-123")
  -> {"status": "running", "latest_turn": 7, "latest_compiler_output": "..."}

Step 4: [wait until complete or failed]
  get_proof_status("abc-123")
  -> {"status": "complete", "proof": "import Mathlib\n...\n  induction n with\n  ..."}

If status=failed:
  list_attempts("abc-123", last_n=5) to inspect what was tried.
  Resubmit with tier=2 or with hints from get_mathlib_search.

## Training wheels — problems in difficulty order

Tier 0 (sanity): trivial arithmetic
  validate_lean("import Mathlib\nexample : 1 + 1 = 2 := by norm_num\n")

Tier 1 (MiniF2F): 488 pre-formalized olympiad problems.
  Clone github.com/leanprover-community/miniF2F and submit files directly via
  submit_lean_file.

Tier 2 (PutnamBench): 658 Putnam competition problems.
  DeepSeek-Prover-V2 671B solves 49/658; good baseline.

Tier 3 (AlphaProof Nexus unsolved): Pre-formalized Lean stubs for 344 unsolved
  Erdos problems at github.com/google-deepmind/alphaproof-nexus-results.
  Submit via submit_lean_file.

Tier 4 (open research): erdosproblems.com ~900 open problems. Requires manual
  Lean formalization of the theorem statement first.

## Key files

src/leanforge_mcp/
  server.py          FastMCP entry point, lifespan, mount composition
  core/
    agent.py         proof loop, statement tamper detection, parallel agents
    lean_client.py   lake env lean subprocess, concurrency semaphore
    llm_client.py    Ollama/DeepSeek/Anthropic, tier escalation
    job_manager.py   SQLite CRUD, job lifecycle, attempt persistence
    runner.py        Runner class, task registry, start_job/cancel
    config.py        TOML loader, typed dataclasses
  tools/
    submit.py        submit_theorem, submit_lean_file
    status.py        get_proof_status, list_attempts, list_jobs, validate_lean
    control.py       cancel_job
    mathlib.py       get_mathlib_search
scripts/
  smoke_test.py      standalone validation, run before anything else
tests/
  test_pipeline.py   pure Python pytest, no Lean needed
docs/
  ALPHAPROOF_NEXUS.md  AlphaProof Nexus paper explained (plain language)
  LEAN.md              Lean 4 language reference, tactic guide, bibliography
  LEAN_PRIMER.md       Quick Lean 4 intro for engineers

## One-time setup required

Before the server will function, run once:
  cd workspace
  lake new leanforge_workspace math
  cd leanforge_workspace
  lake exe cache get    (downloads ~4GB precompiled Mathlib)
  lake build

Then copy config.example.toml to config.toml and set lake_path to the
absolute path of lake.exe (typically C:\Users\{user}\.elan\bin\lake.exe).

## Configuration keys

[lean]
lake_path = path to lake.exe
workspace_dir = path to Lake project with Mathlib
compile_timeout = 120 (seconds per compile)
max_concurrent_compiles = 4 (semaphore gate)

[agent]
parallel_agents = 4
max_turns = 100
escalate_to_tier2_after = 20
escalate_to_tier3_after = 60

[llm.tier1] provider=ollama model=deepseek-prover-v2:7b
[llm.tier2] provider=openai_compat model=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
[llm.tier3] provider=anthropic model=claude-fable-5

[database] path = path to SQLite db file
[server] transport = stdio
[logging] level = INFO
